lines.trans: Still raining outside, Tariq. Will green paint ever dry indoors by Wednesday?
It will if we lay brown paper here and move warm air down the hall.
Water-based garden paint—low smell, fast drying if the air keeps moving.
Where do we point the small fan, Rami?
Crack the courtyard transom two centimetres and blow dry indoor air toward it.
Smart! Steady dry air flows past the wood without letting a drop of rain in.
Look at the colour in the tin when I stir it—deep linden-leaf green!
Thin even strokes along the grain, Nour. Thick paint stays sticky.
First coat before lunch, second coat tonight, rock-hard by Tuesday afternoon!
Hand me the wide brush, Tariq—shutter number one is mine!
Save a small brush for the corners... and somebody watch the door if Mazen walks by.
Too late—here comes Mazen in his clean white Monday shirt!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He called us on Tuesday.
The corner shop is open every Tuesday.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بنية, plural: بنيين).

examples.trans: The brown leather notebook is on the desk.
A clean pair of men's brown shoes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتأخر, بيتأخر).

examples.trans: Tell me I am not late for the lesson!
The bus was not even a minute late.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Describes dry air, dry ingredients, or seasoned dry timber.

examples.text: خلينا نخلي كل المكونات الجافة عالرف العالي.
examples.trans: Let's keep all the dry ingredients on the upper shelf.

examples.text: المفصل بعد ما تدهنه زيت ما بيعود جاف.
examples.trans: Once you oil the hinge, it won't be dry anymore.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a garden or yard; a small one is a جنينة, the formal word is حديقة.

examples.trans: We have a small garden behind the house.
The children are playing in the garden.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Transitive Form II verb ('move furniture, stir a pot, wiggle toes').

examples.text: حركنا البيانو خطوتين لورا بعيد عن الشباك.
examples.trans: We moved the piano two steps back away from the window.

examples.text: حركي الشوربة بملعقة خشب كل خمس دقايق.
examples.trans: Stir the soup with a wooden spoon every five minutes.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Single hinged panel or leaf of a double window, shutter, or cupboard.

examples.text: فتحنا الدرفة الشمال وبعدين الدرفة اليمين.
examples.trans: We swung open the left shutter leaf and then the right one.

examples.text: كل شباك إله درفتين خشب متينات.
examples.trans: Each window has two sturdy wooden shutter panels.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ذكية, plural: أذكياء).

examples.trans: Smart, quick thinking, Nour!
A clever idea solved the problem right away.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Form III verb meaning 'keep a close eye on an oven, timer, or process'.

examples.text: أبو طارق بيراقب درجة حرارة الفرن والمؤقت.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq watches the oven temperature and the timer.

examples.text: أنا براقب من الكرسي وبعطيكم التعليمات.
examples.trans: I'll watch from the chair and give you instructions.

meanings.note: Describes thin flaky pastry, fine paper, or gentle manners.

examples.text: العجينة الرقيقة طلعت مقرمشة وخفيفة بالفرن.
examples.trans: The thin pastry came out crisp and light in the oven.

examples.text: كتب الملاحظة على ورق رقيق بقلم رصاص.
examples.trans: He wrote the note in pencil on thin paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: روايح.

examples.trans: The aroma of coffee in the morning is wonderful!
The scent of cinnamon reaches the second floor.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سميكة, plural: سماك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف السميك هون؟
examples.trans: Who left this thick envelope here?
Thick stone walls hold the warmth.

meanings.note: Shortened in speech to سنتي (dual سنتيين 'two centimetres').

examples.text: قيس المسافة بالمسطرة، لازم تكون عشرة سنتي.
examples.trans: Measure the gap with the ruler—it has to be ten centimetres.

examples.text: كم قميصك بعيد سنتيين بس عن الدهان الرطب!
examples.trans: Your shirt sleeve is only two centimetres from the wet paint!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Collective noun صخر ('solid rock') used in comparisons like ثابت متل الصخر ('steady as a rock').

examples.text: مفصلات الحديد صارت ماكنة وثابتة متل الصخر.
examples.trans: The iron hinges are now sturdy and solid as a rock.

examples.text: بيوت عمان القديمة مبنية على صخر الجبل القوي.
examples.trans: Old Amman houses are built on strong mountain rock.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Instance noun of ضرب; ضربات الفرشاية means 'brushstrokes'.

examples.text: خلي ضربات الفرشاية طويلة وباتجاه عرق الخشب.
examples.trans: Keep the brushstrokes long and in the direction of the wood grain.

examples.text: سمعنا تلات ضربات خفيفة عالباب الخارجي.
examples.trans: We heard three light knocks on the outer door.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عريضة, plural: عراض).

examples.trans: The wide desk under the window is comfortable.
There are wide wooden beams in the ceiling.

meanings.note: Can refer to a cardboard box, a tin can, or a small container.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
I saved this old wooden box.

meanings.note: Contrasts with سفلي / تحتاني ('lower'): الشباك العلوي = 'the upper transom window'.

examples.text: الشباك العلوي فوق الباب مسكر ومحكم عالأخر.
examples.trans: The upper transom window above the door is shut snug and tight.
We lined up the clean glasses on the upper shelf.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Vocalized with kasra to highlight 'grain of wood / vein in stone or leaf'.

examples.text: امشي بالفرشاية مع عرق الخشب مش عكسه.
examples.trans: Move the brush along the wood grain, not against it.

examples.text: خشب الجوز العتيق عروقه غامقة وحلوة كتير.
examples.trans: Vintage walnut wood has dark, beautiful grain lines.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غامقة, plural: غامقين).

examples.trans: The suitcase's color is dark blue.
A dark grey wool coat.

meanings.note: The main meal of the day in Jordan, usually eaten in the early afternoon.

examples.trans: What's for lunch today?
We have lunch together after work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

فرش.gloss: to spread; lay out (cloth or light)

meanings.en: to spread; lay out (cloth or light)
meanings.note: Used literally for spreading a tablecloth or rug and figuratively for warm light spreading across a room.

examples.text: فرشت سلمى شراشف بيضا عالطاولات الخشب.
examples.trans: Salma spread white cloths over the wooden tables.

examples.text: ضو الصبح بيفرش دفا حلو عالساحة.
examples.trans: Morning light spreads lovely warmth across the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a paintbrush, hairbrush, or pastry brush.

examples.text: غسلنا الفرشايات بمي دافية أول ما خلصنا دهان.
examples.trans: We washed the brushes in warm water right after finishing the painting.

examples.text: لا ترفع الإيد اللي ماسكة الفرشاية الخضرا!
examples.trans: Don't lift the hand that's holding the green paintbrush!

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قمصان.

examples.trans: He put on a neat, ironed white shirt.
He changed his shirt twice before the appointment.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Intransitive/transitive verb meaning 'stick fast' (paint on dry wood, stamp on postcard).

examples.text: الدهان ما بيلزق منيح عالخشب المبلول.
examples.trans: Paint does not stick well to wet wood.

examples.text: لزقنا ورقة المواعيد على باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: We stuck the schedule sheet onto the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Compound Levantine interrogative (لـ 'to' + وين 'where').

examples.text: لوين نوجه المروحة عشان ينشف اللوح أسرع؟
examples.trans: Where should we point the fan so the panel dries faster?
Where are you heading in this rain without an umbrella?

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Relates to water, used for colors (light blue/watery), animals, or parks (e.g. water park).

examples.text: الحمد لله الدهان مائي وبيروح بالمي الدافية.
examples.trans: Thankfully the paint is water-based and comes right off with warm water.

examples.text: الدهان المائي ريحته خفيفة وبينشف خلال ساعة.
examples.trans: Water-based paint has a mild smell and dries within an hour.

meanings.note: Form VI active participle meaning 'even in thickness, spacing, or size'.

examples.text: طبقة الدهان طلعت ناعمة ومتساوية من أول لوح لآخره.
examples.trans: The coat of paint came out smooth and even from one end of the panel to the other.

examples.text: قطعنا العجينة لدوائر متساوية لصواني التارت.
examples.trans: We cut the dough into even circles for the tart pans.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمر, بيمر).

examples.trans: Pass right beside the green pharmacy.

examples.text: أنا مريت من جنب السبيل الحجري!
examples.trans: I just passed the stone fountain!

مرق.gloss: to pass by; walk past; drop by

meanings.en: to pass by; walk past; drop by
meanings.note: Quintessential Levantine verb for walking past a street or dropping by.

examples.text: أي حدا بيمرق من شارع الرينبو بيقرأ اللوحة بوضوح.
examples.trans: Anyone walking down Rainbow Street can read the sign clearly.

examples.text: مرق جارنا الساعاتي الصبح وسلم علينا.
examples.trans: Our watchmaker neighbour dropped by in the morning and said hello.

meanings.note: Electric fan or hand fan (from ريح 'wind/breeze').

examples.text: شغلنا المروحة بالممر عشان ينشف الدهان أسرع.
examples.trans: We turned on the fan in the hallway so the paint would dry faster.

examples.text: هوا المروحة الخفيف حرك ريحة الدهان لبرا.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze from the fan carried the paint smell outside.

meanings.note: Standard word for rain, commonly used across all registers of Arabic.

examples.trans: Please come inside out of the cold rain.
The trees are green and lovely after the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمطر, بيمطر).

examples.trans: It is raining outside!
It rained all night in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Standalone معقول! is a classic Jordanian exclamation of amazed disbelief ('No way! / Could it really be?!').

examples.text: معقول! قطار جدي الخشب لسا موجود!
examples.trans: Could it be! Grandfather's wooden train is still around!
The price is reasonable and fair for everyone.

meanings.note: An inside hallway or a narrow passage between buildings.

examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
The hallway is dark, turn on the light.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بناول, بيناول).

examples.trans: Hand me the heavy iron wrench.
Pass me the teacup, please.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb (nishif / byinshaf) meaning 'dry out'.

examples.text: لما تطلع الشمس، الحجار بتنشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: When the sun comes out, the stones dry quickly.

examples.text: استنينا ساعتين لحد ما ينشف الدهان.
examples.trans: We waited two hours until the paint dried.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical dot, a score point, or a drop of liquid.

examples.trans: Not a single drop of juice got on the table!

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من الشوربة السخنة.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the hot soup.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Form II verb disambiguated with shadda from noun وجه ('face').

examples.text: خلينا نوجه المروحة لباب الساحة عشان الهوا يتحرك.
examples.trans: Let's point the fan toward the courtyard door so the air circulates.

examples.text: وجه الضو عاللوحة عشان نشوف الحروف بوضوح.
examples.trans: Point the light at the sign so we can see the letters clearly.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
